criteria.reason: Both plans stay focused on one beginner skill, but B's skill example has a typo ('H, H' instead of 'H—H') and screen 10 adds an unassessed tangent on lone pairs.

A progresses across fresh molecules (H–H, H–Cl, F–F, H₂O, H₂O₂) so the worked example, check, and application test real transfer, whereas B repeats H—H across screens 6–8 (turning the check into recall) and stays on H₂ and H₂O for the whole lesson.

A has one missing visual on screen 8 where the brief asks to show the water model, while B has two visual/activity flaws: repeating the exact same picture with nothing new on screen 5 and using moleculeBuilder twice for H₂O on screens 9 and 11.

Both fit the beginner level and are written in Brazilian Portuguese, each with one minor slip: A uses European-style guillemets on screens 2–4, while B adds an extra out-of-scope screen on lone pairs and angular geometry.

observations.claim: Screen 8 instructs the writer to show the water model with an oxygen atom bonded by a dash to each hydrogen atom, yet sets visual to null (visualKind 'none') and does not even write the inline H–O–H structure.
observations.learnerCost: The writer has no planned visual for the water model, leaving the learner to picture how one oxygen connects to two hydrogens before building it.

location.detail: Mostre no modelo da água um oxigênio (O) ligado por um traço a cada hidrogênio (H).

observations.claim: Screens 2 to 4 use guillemets («elétron», «Ficam em comum», «elétrons compartilhados pelos dois átomos») instead of standard Brazilian Portuguese quotation marks.
observations.learnerCost: If carried into the final lesson, the punctuation will look foreign to Brazilian readers even though the wording and spelling are Brazilian Portuguese.

observations.claim: The skill's example writes 'H, H' with a comma instead of a bond dash ('H—H'), contradicting the notation the skill itself teaches.
observations.learnerCost: A writer or course page relying on the skill example could show the wrong notation to learners.

location.detail: H, H representa dois hidrogênios unidos por um par de elétrons compartilhado.

observations.claim: Screen 6 already introduces H—H, screen 7's worked example walks through H—H again, and screen 8's check asks the learner to represent H—H a third time instead of giving a new similar molecule.
observations.learnerCost: The learner can answer the check by recalling H—H from the previous two screens without practicing applying the rule to a new pair of atoms.

observations.claim: Screen 5 repeats the exact same visual description as screen 4 word for word without adding anything new (such as attraction cues) to illustrate the new electrostatic-attraction idea.
observations.learnerCost: Repeating an identical picture adds no visual clarity for the new concept of attraction between the positive centers and the shared electron pair.

observations.claim: Both screen 9 (explanation) and screen 11 (activity) assign moleculeBuilder for the exact same molecule (H₂O) with the same elements (H and O), duplicating the interaction and giving away screen 11's building task early.
observations.learnerCost: The learner is asked to interact with the same water-building tool twice in three screens rather than seeing a clear diagram once and building the molecule once as practice.

observations.claim: Screen 10 introduces non-bonding electron pairs ('pares não compartilhados') and water's angular shape ('disposição angular'), concepts that are never practiced or checked in this beginner lesson on single covalent bonds.
observations.learnerCost: A beginner has to absorb extra terminology and diagram detail that is never used again in the lesson.

overall.reason: A gives the writer a stronger progression across varied molecules (H–H, H–Cl, F–F, H₂O, and H₂O₂) and cleaner activity design, whereas B turns its worked-example follow-up check into H—H recall, duplicates a picture on screens 4–5, duplicates moleculeBuilder for H₂O, and has a typo in its skill example.

criteria.reason: Both plans are identical in their lesson scope and single skill definition.
A has a wrong answer key on screen 5 claiming total fabric cost stays the same when fewer t-shirts are made, whereas B has the correct answer ('diminuir') and a well-targeted distractor.
Both plans have identical visual decisions (text-only with no decorative pictures) and the same well-chosen categorize activity on screen 8.
Both plans are identical in beginner level, scope, and natural Brazilian Portuguese.

observations.claim: Screen 5 has a wrong answer key: when a sewing workshop makes fewer t-shirts at the same unit fabric price, the total cost of fabric used decreases ('diminuir'), not stays the same ('ficar igual'). Marking 'ficar igual' as correct and 'diminuir' as the distractor directly contradicts the definition of a variable cost taught on screen 2.
observations.learnerCost: The learner will be marked wrong for the right answer and taught the opposite of how variable costs behave.

location.detail: Uma oficina de costura fará menos camisetas, mantendo o tecido e os preços: o custo total do tecido usado vai diminuir, ficar igual ou aumentar? Resposta: ficar igual, porque o preço do tecido não muda; incluir “diminuir” como a resposta tentadora.

overall.reason: The two plans are identical except for screen 5, where A has a major answer-key error that contradicts variable costs and B gets the check right.
